name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Electromagnetic DMR AEDM-3 'Gauss'
description:
The AEDM-3 Gauss is an electromagnetic designated marksman rifle that launches 3mm tungsten penetrators at hypersonic velocity with no chemical propellant and virtually no sound. The weapon's multi-stage electromagnetic acceleration system propels each penetrator to a velocity exceeding Mach 6, creating devastating terminal effects through pure kinetic energy. At the point of impact, the tungsten penetrator releases more energy than a conventional rifle round despite weighing a fraction as much.

The Gauss's silence is its primary tactical advantage. With no propellant gases and no supersonic crack from the barrel (the projectile goes supersonic inside the acceleration chamber), the only sound is the distant impact. A Gauss operator can engage targets at 800 meters with no visible muzzle flash, no sound at the firing position, and no ballistic trail connecting shooter to target. Counter-sniper detection systems designed for chemical-propellant weapons are ineffective.

Arcturus restricts the AEDM-3 to Tier 4+ military contracts at Φ35,000 per unit. The weapon's capacitor system provides 30 shots per charge, and the mandatory BCI link manages the complex acceleration timing that determines projectile velocity and thus effective range. Without the neural interface, the weapon cannot fire.
specifications: caliber: 3mm tungsten penetrator effective_range: 800m rate_of_fire: 30 rpm (capacitor-limited) magazine_capacity: 30 penetrators per charge weight: 5.8 kg (rifle) + 2.0 kg (capacitor pack)
tactical_use: The Gauss provides silent precision fire at distances where conventional suppressed weapons lose effectiveness. Its electromagnetic launch system produces no detectable firing signature, making counter-sniper operations virtually impossible with conventional detection equipment. The tungsten penetrators defeat all personal armor at engagement range. The low rate of fire and limited magazine capacity restrict the weapon to deliberate precision engagement rather than sustained fire support.
cultural_context: The Gauss is a weapon that kills in silence from beyond visual range. Its existence has changed the calculus of outdoor security — any position within 800 meters of potential Gauss deployment must account for a threat that cannot be heard, seen, or conventionally detected. Corporate executives have invested heavily in electromagnetic sensor countermeasures since the Gauss entered service, driving an arms race between silent weapons and detection technology.
story_hooks: A high-profile assassination was committed with a Gauss — no one heard the shot, and the entry wound was so small it was initially missed in the autopsy. Only the tungsten residue identified the weapon type.

Someone has built a makeshift electromagnetic detection array that can identify a Gauss capacitor charging within 200 meters. The technology is crude but functional, and counter-Gauss defense has just become possible.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular designated marksman rifle with a distinctly futuristic profile. The weapon features a pronounced, elongated barrel shroud housing the electromagnetic acceleration chambers. The overall silhouette is svelte and precision-focused, lacking the chunky proportions of chemical-propellant DMRs. Clean lines and minimal protrusions give it an almost surgical appearance.
physical_description.dimensions: 1080mm overall length, 65mm width at receiver, 95mm height with scope rail. Barrel assembly (acceleration chamber) extends 520mm from receiver.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light in hand at 5.8kg (rifle only), with well-distributed balance. The weight shifts slightly forward into the acceleration chamber, but ergonomic design prevents fatigue. Feels precision-engineered rather than hefty.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum-titanium composite frame with reinforced carbon-fiber barrel shroud. Internal electromagnetic components mounted in hardened steel staging rings.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed titanium accents around the receiver and acceleration chamber ports. Wear-resistant DLC (diamond-like carbon) coating on all handling surfaces to minimize fingerprints and thermal signature.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with silver-gray highlights. Capacitor pack connector glows faint blue when charged.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with integrated pressure-sensitive panels that interface with the BCI link. Slight grip knurling for secure purchase even with tactical gloves.
distinctive_features: Three visible electromagnetic coil stages along the barrel shroud, each marked with faint circular indent patterns
Capacitor connection port at rear receiver (glows faint cyan when energized)
Minimal aperture sight rails; designed for integrated BCI targeting overlay
Ventilation ports along the barrel shroud for thermal management of acceleration coils
No muzzle brake or suppressor—acceleration occurs entirely within the shroud
Neural interface contact points on the charging handle (subtle gold-plated contacts)
Tungsten penetrator magazine mounted horizontally below the receiver, translucent polymer showing 3mm round profile
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions engraved in small caps along the left side of the receiver. Iron Point Ammunition maker's mark stamped on the capacitor pack. Serial plate recessed into the stock with encrypted QR encoding.
physical_description.condition_typical: Immaculate in-contract service. Weapons are maintained to exacting standards and rarely see field abuse due to their restricted military deployment. Typically shows zero to minimal wear; any visible damage indicates heavy combat history.
